## Objective
- Continue the existing project and deliver a complete, playable game or improve the current game without asking questions.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The repository already contains a Three.js kart-racing game, so the work began by inspecting and validating that game rather than replacing it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3002 and installed Chromium for Playwright.
- Loaded the game and captured `/tmp/opencode/turbo-current.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- Investigate and fix why `styles.css` appears truncated in the browser: only six CSS rules are parsed, ending at `.vignette`, so the HUD, title screen, and controls lack their intended styling.
- The CSS file itself appears to contain the full stylesheet through its final media query; determine why parsing stops after the `.vignette` rule.

### Blocked
- The title/HUD are currently unstyled in the browser because the stylesheet parser stops after the sixth rule; no code changes have been made yet.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the browser’s response for `styles.css` and identify any malformed content or truncation causing CSS parsing to stop.
2. Fix the stylesheet issue, reload, and inspect a new JPEG screenshot.
3. Test the start flow and basic driving controls; then summarize the result and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Intended game visuals; browser currently parses only its first six rules.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, start and finish screens, and control elements.
- `game.js`: Existing Three.js circuit, race logic, keyboard and touch controls.

## Important Context
- Browser check: `playwright-cli eval` reported only six CSS rules, with the last parsed rule `.vignette { position: absolute; inset: 0px; pointer-events: none; }`.
- `styles.css` on disk is 10,986 bytes and visibly contains rules after `.vignette`, including `.topbar`, `.race-hud`, `.screen`, and responsive media queries.
- Browser console’s initial error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404); other entries were SwiftShader `GPU stall due to ReadPixels` warnings.
